profile.name: Piyush Mourya
profile.intro_summary: I'm Piyush, an AI engineer and builder based in Bengaluru, focusing heavily on agentic AI architectures and LLM systems. I graduated from IIT Bombay in Engineering Physics, and I enjoy building production software from mathematical first-principles.

education.foundation: First-principles thinking, problem solving, mathematical physics, statistical mechanics, competitive math (2000+ rating)
education.transition_to_ai: Engineering Physics at IIT Bombay built my core foundation in mathematical modeling and statistical physics, which naturally transitioned into designing complex agentic workflows and AI system architectures.

lifestyle.fitness: Regular gym workouts and staying healthy
hobbies: Tracking tech trends, internet memes, and global politics

interview_pillars.superpower: My number one superpower is my drive for knowledge. I genuinely believe knowledge is power; once I understand the fundamentals of a problem, I gain the confidence to tackle it and deliver on my promises without hesitation.
interview_pillars.strength: My biggest strength is that I'm confident, dependable, and I consistently deliver on what I promise.
interview_pillars.weakness: My biggest weakness is perfectionism. Wanting everything to be completely flawless can sometimes slow down shipping things that would be better off delivered earlier with faster iteration.
interview_pillars.growth_areas: The top three areas I'm actively working to grow in are: first, getting deeper hands-on experience on the DevOps side of infrastructure. Second, mastering low-level system design and performance optimization, like low-latency databases. And third, diving deeper into classical machine learning, because in many real-world problems, classical ML is actually more effective and practical than Gen AI.
interview_pillars.pushing_limits: I push my limits by throwing myself into unfamiliar domains until I build something real—whether that was robotics at IIT Roorkee, contributing upstream to Google ADK, or hacking hardware controllers for my room.
interview_pillars.coworker_misconception: People sometimes assume my physics and competitive math background makes me purely theoretical. In reality, I'm an obsessive builder who cares deeply about shipping production code, reliability, and rock-solid tests.

flagship_enterprise.name: Enterprise Metadata Query Platform
flagship_enterprise.business_problem: B2B enterprise clients had vast metadata already unified and ingested from 20 to 30+ separate systems into a 7TB backend, but the dashboard was too crowded and complex for non-technical users to easily check data lineage, ownership, or redundancy.
flagship_enterprise.solution: Built the agentic natural-language query bot and MCP tool layer sitting on top of that existing 7TB backend, so users can ask questions in plain English and get instant answers with direct links back to the dashboard. Did NOT build the data ingestion pipelines itself.

architecture_7TB.postgresql: Stored the core bulk relational metadata records and asset attributes.
architecture_7TB.elasticsearch: Used for lightning-fast search of asset IDs, parent IDs, system instances, and popular UI assets.
architecture_7TB.falkordb: Redis Graph extension used specifically to trace graphical Data Lineage and asset dependencies across systems.
architecture_7TB.mcp_tool_layer: Custom MCP tools doing single-database lookups and multi-database tool chaining to answer complex questions.

personal_build.name: OneSearchGo
personal_build.motivation: I do daily journaling and life-logging, but it was really difficult to piece together personal information across voice dumps, call logs, SMS, and screenshots.
personal_build.how_it_works: A strictly private personal life-logging search engine. Users dump their own SMS, voice notes, screenshots, and logs into a local pgvector store, and a 4-tool agentic loop does fast semantic and SQL retrieval. CRITICAL: It does ZERO web crawling or web searches—it is 100% grounded on personal dumped data only.

open_source.name: Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)
open_source.contribution: Implemented Model Context Protocol (MCP) sampling support in Google's Agent Development Kit (merged via PR #4718), allowing MCP tools to request LLM completions directly from the client.
